shortDescription: Create and manage API keys for elastic.

options.name: api_key_encoded
options.description: API key credentials which is the Base64-encoding of the UTF-8\ representation of the id and api_key joined by a colon (:). Supported from Elastic 8+. See [Create API Key](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/security-api-create-api-key.html) documentation for specifics.

options.name: expiration
options.description: The expiration time for the API key. By default, API keys never expire. Accepts various time units e.g. 7d, 1M, 24h.

options.name: login_hosts
options.description: The Elastic hosts to connect to. Can accept hostnames or URLs. If a hostname then values\ login_port and login_scheme will be used to construct a URL.

options.name: login_password
options.description: The password used to authenticate with. Required when I(login_user) is specified.

options.name: login_port
options.description: The Elastic server port to login to.

options.name: login_user
options.description: The Elastic user to login with. Required when I(login_password) is specified.

options.name: metadata
options.description: Arbitrary metadata that you want to associate with the API key. It supports nested data structure.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the API key.

options.name: role_descriptors
options.description: An array of role descriptors for this API key. When it is not specified or it is an empty array, the API key will have a point in time snapshot of permissions of the authenticated user.

options.name: state
options.description: The required state of the API key. It is not possible to hard delete a \ api key, so they are expired, Elastic \ will clean them up at some point. This means that you will encounter problems \ when attempting to quicky delete and recreate \ api keys with the same name. Api Keys cannot be updated after creation via this module.
